audit.whatIsWrong: The two-item row is printed as Skill in both layers while whys[6] says 'he owns this window, so splitpush instead', spikes[3] says the kill threat dies and he facetanks your full combo, and late says 'This is where it flips and you have to be honest about it.' The packet levelChart and the mirror findings both give that row to Dr. Mundo. Row 3 (Levels 4-5) is printed as Fiora at 7/10 while whys[3] ends 'skill matchup' and the packet says Skill.
audit.why: The final row is the one the whole page builds toward — 'close the game before two items plus Maximum Dosage make him unkillable' — and the chart was printing it as an even fight.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Fiora 7 / Fiora 7 / Fiora 7 / Skill 5 / Skill 5 / Skill 5 / Dr. Mundo 4 in both layers; phases[3..6].why rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why claimed Grand Challenge 'wins any committed duel' and phases[5].why claimed 'Ravenous Hydra is your spike — force fights the moment it completes', both on rows the content layer calls even.
audit.why: At 6 the heal zone is a window rather than a kill because his passive regen answers it, and at first item he is one purchase away from out-healing your DPS. Both rows are races against sustain, not free commits.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why and phases[5].why now state the race rather than promising the kill.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer describes Heart Zapper only as 'His sustain spike + reset' and never says what it actually does, and NOTHING anywhere on the page mentions Goes Where He Pleases resisting the first immobilizing effect that hits him.
audit.why: Heart Zapper stores a portion of the damage he takes and heals him a percentage of it when the burst lands — so every point you pour into him during those seconds partially refunds. Breaking contact before the recast is the concrete rule, and it is nowhere on the page. His passive is bigger still for point 8: it eats the first immobilize outright, so a jungler's engage CC is absorbed unless something cheap is spent first. The content layer correctly notes he has no immobilizing CC for you to parry, but never notes that he negates yours.
audit.corrected: Heart Zapper's stored-damage heal and 17s rank-1 cooldown written into breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, dosFull[0].d and dontsFull[2].d; Maximum Dosage's missing-health heal into dosFull[2].d; Infected Bonesaw's 975 range, 4s cooldown and health cost into dontsFull[1].d; the passive's first-immobilize resist into report[10].t as a jungle instruction.

audit.whatIsWrong: The jungle section said only 'ping your jungler when Heart Zapper is down', which is generic and, in this specific matchup, misleading.
audit.why: Goes Where He Pleases absorbs the first immobilizing effect. A jungler who opens a gank with their hard CC gets it eaten and the dive fails. Spending a cheap CC or an auto-attack first is what makes the gank work.
audit.corrected: report[10].t replaced with the passive rule.

notes: Highest-value addition here is Goes Where He Pleases: nothing on the page mentioned that his passive resists the first immobilizing effect, which changes how every gank on this lane has to be sequenced. It now sits in report[10].t. Second is Heart Zapper, which the full layer described only as 'sustain spike + reset' — it actually banks a portion of the damage he takes and refunds him a share of it on the burst, so the rule is to break contact before the recast. The content layer here is unusually good and already states the Riposte condition correctly ('W only returns a stun if you parry an immobilizing effect'), so I left it alone apart from the chart. Carried forward the mirror's caution on the damage type of a passive Vital hit: Riot's text says only that it restores health and grants move speed, and the trueDamage flag sits on Grand Challenge, so I neither repeated nor removed the page's 'Vital true damage' phrasing.
